entries.gave: Read the Cut, invoicer as it stands (command.py, lines.py, render.py, totals.py, tax.py, __init__.py, tests, pyproject.toml) and the two Mores kept. Its people: colleagues from accounting, who run `invoicer LINES --rate PERCENT` on the lines saved from their spreadsheet and get the invoice to send, and code that calls the package as it called 1.4.0. The Mores: a whole-number price stops render, subtotal and total with AttributeError in tax.to_cent; `--rate 19 --rate 7` quietly prints at 7%.
Read code/best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-code/best-practice.md, to their end, before any change.

Decided: the Cut decisions as they stand. Settled without asking: (1) tax.to_cent reads the amount by Decimal(amount), exact for a whole number, so Line keeps the price it was given, as 1.4.0 did, and render, subtotal, total and tax_of take a whole-number price; (2) --rate is kept by action append and refused in main where given more than once, with the message: argument --rate: the tax rate is given more than once; give it once, such as --rate 19.

Specification: the unit cases in tests/test_command.py, test_lines.py and test_totals.py, plus the two the Cut adds: render, subtotal and total of a line with a whole-number price, and a rate given twice refused.
Left to the code: where a whole-number price becomes a Decimal (in Line, or where it is rounded), and how argparse sees a second --rate (append, or an Action of its own).

The rounding to the cent stays with tax.py, so the whole-number price is read there; Line keeps the price as given, as 1.4.0 did. The refusal of a second --rate stays with command.py, which decides what the command takes. No module added.
No decision has variants that the cases call for; no pattern added.
Offered names unchanged: Line, LineError, parse_lines, render, subtotal, tax_of, total, and main; no name added.
Each change traces to a case: Decimal(amount) in to_cent to the whole-number price cases, action append with one check in main to the rate given twice. No other option or branch planned.

Cases designed: test_render_prints_a_line_whose_price_is_a_whole_number, test_subtotal_of_a_line_whose_price_is_a_whole_number, test_total_of_a_line_whose_price_is_a_whole_number, supporting test_prints_the_invoice_of_the_lines_at_the_rate_given; and test_refuses_a_rate_given_twice in test_command.py.
No case needed that supports no unit case; nothing to ask.
Inputs from outside: LINES and --rate, read in command.main; --rate is now kept each time it is given, and refused before the file is read where given more than once.
Test command from pyproject.toml: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.
pyproject.toml gives the command, so no search for a runner was needed.
66 tests pass before any change, in a throwaway copy.
Things handled: the line, its price, its amount, the rate; each has one name in the code.
The Cut says the tax rate and the price, as the code and its messages do.
No two names for one thing found; the new message says the tax rate, as the other --rate messages do.
No name used for two things found.
The rounding to the cent is written in tax.to_cent alone; totals.line_amount and tax_of call it.
No look-alike places to take apart for these changes.
tax.py keeps the reading of an amount to round, as it keeps the rounding; nothing written twice.
Kinds done in many places: refusing an input of the command, and rounding an amount.
Refusals in command.py all go through parser.error or ArgumentTypeError; rounding goes through tax.to_cent.
The rate given twice is refused through parser.error with argument --rate:, the way nearest it, as the other rate refusals read.
No new way chosen.
Openings kept, each naming its decision; totals.py adds that each function takes a price that is a Decimal or a whole number and gives a Decimal.

From the openings alone: a change of how an amount is rounded names tax.py; a change of what --rate takes names command.py; a new field of a line names lines.py; a new row of the invoice names render.py.
Line takes price: Decimal | int and amount() gives Decimal | int; the older tax.py stays without hints, as the Cut leaves the type hints of the older modules out.
Docstrings now say: Line and to_cent take a Decimal or a whole number; render and the totals take lines whose price is either; main refuses --rate given more than once.
Checked each new test against its interface: the whole-number price and the refusal of a second --rate are both in the docstrings they call.
Least code for each test: Decimal(amount) in to_cent for the three whole-number price tests; action append and one len check in main for the rate given twice.
Ran the tests after the code: 70 tests pass.
Read the changed bodies: no option, mode or branch that no case calls for.
pyproject.toml unchanged: Python 3.9 or later, no other package, the test command in its head comment.
The new command test saves its file in the temporary folder of its own setUp; the totals tests use no file.
The tests run no real tool beyond Python.
Ran the 70 tests in three shuffled orders, seeds 11, 22 and 33: each passes.

In a throwaway copy with an empty home, pip install --target from the setup alone gave bin/invoicer, and the tests copied out of the repository passed against the installed package. A venv could not be made there, as ensurepip is missing on this machine.
Wrote one test for each designed case, beside the cases they support: three in tests/test_totals.py, one in tests/test_command.py; no name needs and.
Expected values from each Then: 50 times 2 is 100.00, 19 percent of it 19.00, the total 119.00; the refusal message as decided in step 3.
Each new test keeps its line, price and rates in its own body; only the existing saved and run_command helpers are shared.
No loop or branch in the new tests.
The new tests compare whole values whose names and comments say what they check; no further failure message needed.

Ran the four new tests before the code: the three whole-number price tests failed with AttributeError int has no quantize, and test_refuses_a_rate_given_twice with exit 0 and the invoice printed, each the reason its Then names.
The new tests use the real modules and a file in their own temporary folder; no test double.
The new tests call Line, render, subtotal and total from invoicer, and main from invoicer.command; nothing internal.
Renamed the internal _rate to _percent_rate in a throwaway copy: all tests still pass.
Each new test asserts the whole result: all printed rows, the full subtotal and total, and the exit code, the empty output and the whole message.
coverage.py is not on this machine, so lines were measured by python3 -m trace: the only unrun line in the package is Line.__repr__, there before this round; every changed line runs.
Line.__repr__ serves a caller reading a Line, a behavior of 1.4.0 that this round leaves as it was; no line of this round goes unrun.
No Test strategy names an interface for property-based tests; none written.
No property-based test, so no failing input to weigh.
The round takes no CI report of mutation testing; no mutant to list.
No mutant listed, so nothing to remove.
No mutant listed, so none to mark.
No mutant listed, so no test to tighten.
Every --rate is read through _rate into a fraction where it comes in; main then takes only a list of one rate on to the invoice.
Two rates can not be read in one way, so the command refuses them instead of taking the last.
No new catch; Decimal() of a whole number raises nothing to catch.
The message names the program, the option, what is wrong and what it takes: invoicer: error: argument --rate: the tax rate is given more than once; give it once, such as --rate 19.
The check is an if that calls parser.error, so it runs under python -O too.

Ran the installed invoicer with --rate 19 --rate 7 and with --rate=19 --rate=19: exit 2, no invoice, and the message alone says to give the rate once; --rate 0.19 --rate 7 names the fraction first, as each value is read where it comes in.
Searched tests for to_cent, tax_of, Line and the --rate option: no test reached a whole-number price or a second --rate.
Both were behaviors to change, not to pin, as the Cut decides them; their tests assert the decided behavior, the 1.4.0 one for a whole-number price.
Small steps: to_cent first, then the --rate append with its check, then the docstrings, the tests run after each.
No name renamed; no expected result of an existing test changed.
The tests ran after each step: the 66 existing tests pass throughout, 70 with the new ones.

Callers now get what 1.4.0 gave for a whole-number price: Line keeps the price as given, and render, subtotal, total and tax_of give Decimals to the cent. No other behavior looks wrong against the Cut.
No function, class or constant added that nothing names.
No function added that only passes the call on.
No parameter added.
The two comments added say what the code cannot: why Decimal() wraps the amount, and why --rate is appended.
The new local rate, read in main, holds the one tax rate given.
Its definition, arguments.rate[0] after the check, matches; arguments.rate now holds a list, read only in main, two lines from where it is set.
No name differs from the word kept; nothing renamed.
main: reads the rate and the lines from the command line and prints their invoice, refusing a wrong one. to_cent: rounds an amount half up to the cent. Each new test: one call and its whole result.
No line stopped the reading.
The sentences need no and that joins tasks a caller would want apart.
Nothing outside each function was needed for its sentence.
main keeps one level: each check is a step of reading the command line.
No function with one caller and no name of its own added.
Marked as looking roundabout: Decimal() of what may already be a Decimal, and action append on an option taken once.
No name of a few words says either reason, so each has a comment.

Comments from the Cut decisions: in to_cent, Decimal() reads a whole number exactly, as a line built with a price such as 50 gives one; on --rate, each is kept so that main refuses a second, where argparse would take the last.
Every reason was found in the Cut; nothing left to ask.
Docstrings corrected to what the code now does: Line, to_cent, render and the totals opening name a whole-number price; main names a rate given more than once.
The reading of an amount for rounding is written once, in tax.to_cent, which line_amount and tax_of both call.
No flag-picked branch added.
No code uses another module internal name.
No rule written in two languages by this round.
The new refusal is written as the others in command.py, by parser.error with argument --rate:.
No place keeps a different way.

Made: tax.to_cent reads the amount by Decimal(), so render, subtotal, total and tax_of take a whole-number price; command.py keeps each --rate and refuses a second before reading the file; docstrings of Line, to_cent, render, totals and main say so; four tests added, 70 pass.

Tried in throwaway copies with an empty home, installed by pip install --target from the setup alone: a file saved as CSV UTF-8 with a byte order mark, a quoted cell, a whole-number price and a discount prints the invoice to the cent, exit 0; --rate 19 --rate 7 and --rate=19 --rate=19 exit 2 with no invoice and the one-line message; subtotal and total of Line("Hosting", 50, 1) give 50.00 and 59.50; 70 tests pass, also in three shuffled orders and against the installed package.
Wrote the Made in rounds/invoicer/5/made.json: where each of the ten decisions is carried out, where the two Mores kept are made good, and the two points settled without asking, each with its ground.
Made written; ending with done once the check gives 0.
